title: MTEL Physical Education (22) Practice Test - MTEL - Human Growth and Development
subject: MTEL

questions.q: Which of the following intellectual milestones is most closely associated with the adolescent stage of human growth and development?
options: becoming interested in abstract ideas and the process of thinking itself
operational thinking that allows one to mentally combine, order, and transform objects and actions
learning to take intentions into account in judging the behaviors of others
representing reality to oneself through the use of symbols, gestures, and mental images
questions.explain: During adolescence, students develop advanced reasoning skills and the ability to think abstractly and in hypothetical terms. The other options describe cognitive milestones that typically occur at younger ages.
questions.subject: MTEL

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the usual progression of physical growth in infants and toddlers?
options: Physical growth occurs first in the lower body and proceeds upward to the torso and head.
Physical growth occurs in all major regions of the body simultaneously at about the same rate.
Physical growth occurs first in the head and proceeds downward to the trunk and outward toward the extremities.
Physical growth occurs variably in individuals with no typical starting point or progression of growth.
questions.explain: Physical growth in infants and toddlers follows two main patterns: the **cephalocaudal pattern** (head to foot) and the **proximodistal pattern** (center outward). This means growth starts at the head and proceeds downward and outward.
questions.subject: MTEL

questions.q: In general, heredity plays the largest role in influencing which area of personal growth and development?
options: body type and composition
susceptibility to stress-related illnesses
degree of strength and flexibility that can be achieved with fitness training
quality of relationships with friends, teachers, and classmates
questions.explain: An individual's body type and composition (the proportion of fat, muscle, and bone) are determined to a large degree by heredity and genetics, although environmental factors also play a role.
questions.subject: MTEL

questions.q: During an adolescent growth spurt in which a student's arms and legs grow longer, the proportion of limb-to-torso-length often changes, resulting in:
options: significant increases in joint flexibility.
periods of poor coordination and balance.
significant decreases in connective tissue elasticity.
immediate improvement in technical skill and control.
questions.explain: During a rapid adolescent growth spurt, bone growth can outpace muscle and tendon development. This shift in the body's proportions and center of gravity can lead to a temporary period of clumsiness, poor coordination, and balance issues.
questions.subject: MTEL

questions.q: The activity patterns of five- and six-year-old children are likely to be more physically demanding than the activity patterns of younger children mainly because of improvements in:
options: gross-motor skills.
cardiorespiratory function.
manipulative skills.
involuntary reflexes.
questions.explain: By ages five and six, children have developed greater facility with gross-motor skills (large muscle actions like running, jumping, and turning). This improved motor control, strength, and balance enables them to participate in more complex and physically demanding activities.
questions.subject: MTEL

questions.q: During which stage of growth and development are total daily caloric needs greatest?
options: infancy
early childhood
adolescence
early adulthood
questions.explain: Adolescence is a period of rapid growth, second only to infancy. Due to this growth spurt and increases in body size and muscle mass, total daily caloric needs are higher during adolescence than at any other point in the lifespan.
